episodes.188153: During the late afternoon into early evening hours of March 5th, slow moving to nearly stationary thunderstorms caused periods of heavy rain across south central Indiana with pockets of flash flooding in both Washington, Indiana and southwestern Greene County. Rain gauges reported up to 3.75 inches of rainfall near these areas of flash flooding.
episodes.188174: Scattered thunderstorms developed on March 6 and caused flooding in several areas. The most intense flooding occurred near Salinas and Prunedale, where a stationary thunderstorm developed around 12 Noon. This storm produced torrential rainfall with one observer in North Salinas reporting 1 of rain in 25 minutes.
episodes.188759: Thunderstorms embedded within a squall line associated with a mesoscale convective system produce gusty winds across Tampa Bay waters.
episodes.188800: An upper level trough destabilized the atmosphere and led to heavy rain that caused isolated flooding impacts on the Big Island.
episodes.188846: A cluster of showers and thunderstorms with gusty winds moved across the coastal waters with a wind gust of 36 knots measured on Dog Island.
episodes.189555: During the evening hours on the 5th, a slow-moving frontal band of showers and thunderstorms oriented SW to NE was drifting southeastward across the Ohio River. A thunderstorm developed in SE portions of Henderson County, moving northwestward. As the storm collided with the line, locally heavy rainfall occurred over the city of Henderson, which led to flooding issues necessitating the closure of multiple roads.
episodes.189867: As a mid-level trough moved over the Florida Peninsula, abundant low-level moisture and diurnal heating led to plenty of instability in the atmosphere on March 6th. Scattered showers and thunderstorms formed in the afternoon and evening across the metro areas of Southeast Florida.
episodes.189868: A large mesoscale convective system (MCS) associated with a mid-level shortwave brought numerous showers and thunderstorms to South Florida during the early morning hours of March 6th, with a few strong thunderstorms across Miami-Dade County.
episodes.190183: As a weak area of low pressure moved northeastward along the South Carolina coast, clusters of thunderstorms tracked across the adjacent Atlantic coastal waters. These thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts as they moved to the northeast.
episodes.190198: Early morning thunderstorms moving offshore produced strong wind gusts at the coast.
episodes.190496: A deep trough brought widespread hail showers and snow to Northwest California. Heavy snow of several feet was measured in the mountains while the hail showers resulted in numerous traffic accidents along the coast.
episodes.191610: An offshore low pressure system advecting cooler drier air while a series of shortwave disturbances enhance precipitation.
